property_summary: After calling transferOwnership and then owned, the owner address changes to the new owner in P but stays the same in M.
After a call to transferOwnership by the owner, the owner changes to the new address in P but stays unchanged in M; then owned() reverts for the old owner in P but succeeds in M.

After a non-owner calls transferOwnership(address(1)), the owner changes to address(1); then owned() reverts on the reference (since onlyOwner modifier prevents non-owner) but succeeds on the buggy version (which no longer checks owner)—the assertion that owned() does not revert fails for the bug.

A non-owner calls transferOwnership to set a new owner, then calls owned(); the reference reverts because onlyOwner blocks non-owner, but the buggy version succeeds, so the test asserts that owned() does not revert.

After a non-owner calls transferOwnership(address(0)), the owner changes to address(0); then owned() reverts on the reference (since onlyOwner allows only the current owner, address(0), to call it) but succeeds on the buggy version (which removed the onlyOwner check), so the assertion that owned() does not revert fails for the bug.
After a non-owner calls transferOwnership(address(1)), the reference reverts when a non-owner calls owned(), but the buggy version succeeds; the test asserts that owned() does not revert.

Non-owner calls transferOwnership to set owner to address(0), then calls owned(); the reference reverts (onlyOwner modifier checks owner==msg.sender, but owner is address(0) and msg.sender is non-owner, so revert), while the buggy version does not check the modifier and succeeds. The assertion checks that owned() does not revert, which fails on the reference but passes on the buggy version.
